sections.h2: Where is Pueblo County and what is in it?
sections.html:
Pueblo County sits in south central Colorado, and its county seat and largest city is Pueblo. The county covers 2,398 square miles, of which about 12 are water, and it was founded on November 1, 1861.

It borders El Paso County to the north, Fremont and Custer counties to the west, Huerfano and Las Animas counties to the south, and Otero, Crowley and Lincoln counties to the east. The 2020 census counted 168,162 residents, and about 86.9% of them live in urban areas, so most homeowners here sit inside the city of Pueblo or its edges.

Landmarks include the brass-domed county courthouse, Lake Pueblo State Park, the Historic Arkansas Riverwalk and the Union Avenue Historic Commercial District. For a seller, a house in the city, a rural lot on the plains and a place near the lake each come with different services, so confirm which taxing districts apply to your parcel.

sections.h2: Who are the biggest employers around Pueblo?
sections.html:
Health care, government, education and heavy industry lead the list. The city's 2023 annual financial report, as summarized by Wikipedia, puts UCHealth Parkview Medical Center first at 4,293 employees.

EmployerEmployees (2023)
UCHealth Parkview Medical Center4,293
Colorado Mental Health Hospital in Pueblo2,000
Pueblo School District 601,677
Colorado State University Pueblo1,500
Walmart (county-wide)1,493
Evraz Rocky Mountain Steel931

Steel built the city. The Colorado Fuel and Iron mill was the state's largest employer for nearly a century, and the 1982 steel crash hit local households hard. Solar and wind equipment manufacturing now appears among the other notable sectors. Job concentration in a few large institutions means a sale that follows a layoff, a transfer or a retirement is a common story here.

sections.h2: How does Pueblo's climate affect a house and its tax value?
sections.html:
Pueblo is semi-arid, with roughly 12 inches of precipitation a year and close to 3,470 hours of sunshine. Summers are hot and dry, with highs of 90 degrees Fahrenheit or more on about 72 days a year, and winters are mild, with about 28 inches of snow in a season.

That mix is hard on roofing and exterior paint, and a house with an older cooling system or thin attic insulation costs more to run. The record high is 109 degrees (July 13, 2003) and the record low is minus 31 (February 1, 1951), so both ends of the range test a building.

Flooding has a long history in town. The Great Flood of 1921 destroyed roughly one third of downtown businesses, and the Riverwalk now documents it. If your parcel is near the Arkansas River or Fountain Creek, ask your insurer about flood coverage before you list.

sections.h2: Which Pueblo County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Two offices do the work: the Assessor values and classifies every property, and the Treasurer bills and collects the tax. Both are in the Pueblo County Historical Courthouse at 215 W. 10th Street, Pueblo, CO 81003.

OfficeWhat it doesPhone
AssessorValues and lists real and personal property, keeps ownership and lot records719-583-6597
Treasurer, Revenue DepartmentTakes tax payments, handles abatements, mails statements719-583-6690
Treasurer, Tax CertificationIssues tax certifications for title companies and lenders719-583-6682
Treasurer, RedemptionDelinquent tax payments, tax lien sales, elderly tax deferral719-583-6689

The Assessor also keeps the ownership, legal description and lot size records for the county, and the property search tool on the Assessor page lets you check your parcel before you talk to a buyer. Mobile and manufactured homes are taxed too, and the Treasurer issues the moving permits for them.

The Treasurer's office is on the first floor and is open 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, except holidays. The Assessor does not send the tax bill, so questions about an amount due go to the Treasurer.

sections.h2: What are the Pueblo County protest and appeal steps?
sections.html:
You protest your value to the Assessor first, then appeal to the County Board of Equalization (CBOE) if you still disagree. Real property is revalued in odd-numbered years, and the Assessor mails Notices of Valuation by May 1.

  • The Assessor's 2025 procedures set a June 8 deadline for protests by mail (postmarked), in person or by email, and say the right to protest is lost after that date.
  • A protest should include your own estimate of value as of June 30, 2024, plus any documents that support a change.
  • The Assessor must mail a Notice of Determination on or before the last working day in June.
  • To continue, file a written appeal with the CBOE by July 15 under C.R.S. 39-8-106.

The county's Board of Equalization page lists different dates, with a May 31 protest deadline and hearings from July 15 to August 5. Because the two county pages do not agree, read the dates printed on your own notice. Hearings run 20 minutes, split between you and the Assessor, and cannot be rescheduled once set.

sections.h2: When is Pueblo County property tax due, and what if it goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Colorado property tax bills are paid in full by April 30 or in two halves, the first by the last day of February and the second by June 15. Bills of $25 or less are due in full by April 30.

The state sets residential assessment rates by class. For 2026 the guide published by Larimer County lists 6.8% for local governments and 7.05% for schools on residential property. Your bill is the assessed value multiplied by the combined mill levies of each district.

Unpaid tax can end in a tax lien sale, which the Treasurer's Redemption Department manages. The Treasurer has also announced that its Treasurer's Deed auction bidding rules and fees have changed. Other help exists: Pueblo's Property Tax Work Off Program gives volunteers a voucher toward the January payment, and the Redemption Department runs the deferral program for older residents.

sections.h2: How do back taxes work when you sell a Pueblo County house?
sections.html:
Taxes for the year of sale are normally settled at closing, and the title company asks the Treasurer for a tax certification. Pueblo's Tax Certification Department issues those certifications for title companies and lending institutions.

  • Ask the title company to order the certification early so any delinquency shows up before the closing date.
  • Any tax still owed is paid from the sale proceeds, so a lien does not need to stop a sale.
  • The deed is recorded with the county, and a transfer deed over $500 carries the state documentary fee of $.01 per $100, as the Boulder County recorder describes it.

If the bill is large and the house needs work, a cash sale as is can shorten the path, since there is no lender appraisal to wait for. We can walk through your Pueblo County tax figures with you before you decide anything.

faqs.q: Who sends the Pueblo County property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Pueblo County Treasurer collects and bills the tax. The Assessor only sets the value, so call the Treasurer's Revenue Department at 719-583-6690 about an amount due.

faqs.q: What is the Pueblo County protest deadline?
faqs.a: The Assessor's 2025 procedures give June 8 for mailed, in person and emailed protests. The county Board of Equalization page lists May 31, so check the date on your Notice of Valuation.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Pueblo County house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid amount is normally paid from the sale proceeds at closing, and the title company gets a tax certification from the Treasurer to show the exact figure.

faqs.q: How many people live in Pueblo County?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 168,162 residents, with a 2025 estimate of 169,277. The city of Pueblo had 111,876 residents in 2020.
Pueblo School District 60 covers almost all of the city limits, and Pueblo County School District 70 covers very small portions. Your tax bill lists the school levy that applies to your parcel.

faqs.q: Does Pueblo County have help for older homeowners with tax bills?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's Redemption Department manages a tax deferral program for the elderly, and the county runs a Property Tax Work Off Program where volunteer hours earn a voucher.
